beginner.headline: Oil Kills Birds and Closes Park
beginner.brief: A bird park in County Antrim has closed while workers remove oil from its pond. Someone damaged a nearby oil tank, and oil from it killed 13 birds. The oil was a type that people use to heat their homes. More than 20 birds went to an animal care centre for special help. The team is helping geese, ducks and swans. They washed the birds and gave them special care as quickly as possible. The water is much cleaner now, but workers still need to do more. Most birds at the centre cannot return until the pond is completely clean. Police are asking people to share any information about what happened.

intermediate.headline: Oil Spill Kills Birds and Forces Wildlife Park Closure
intermediate.brief: Deliberate damage to a home heating tank caused an oil spill that killed 13 birds from Broughshane Waterfowl Park. The attraction in County Antrim has been forced to close while teams continue to remove oil from its pond. More than 20 birds were taken for urgent specialist treatment, but the number of deaths has continued to rise. A volunteer arriving to feed the birds noticed an oil smell and saw black swans covered in oil. The park keeps 120 birds and also provides a home for wild birds. Environmental inspectors used special floating barriers that absorb oil to limit the damage to the ponds. The waterway has improved considerably, although further work will continue for as long as necessary. Rescue workers have bathed and treated the affected birds as quickly as possible because of the oil pollution. The team also gave the birds charcoal to help fight harmful substances they had swallowed. Birds can hide signs of illness, so symptoms may only become clear when it is too late. Most rescued birds are not native to the area, so they cannot return until the pond is completely clean. Police have appealed for anyone with information about the incident to come forward.

advanced.headline: Oil Tank Vandalism Kills Birds at Broughshane Waterfowl Park
advanced.brief: Vandalism of a nearby home heating oil tank caused a spill that killed 13 birds from Broughshane Waterfowl Park. More than 20 birds were taken to the USPCA's headquarters for emergency treatment, yet the death toll continued to rise. The attraction in County Antrim remains closed while work to remove oil from its pond continues. A volunteer arriving to feed the birds noticed a kerosene smell and found the black swans coated in oil. The park houses 120 birds in its collection as well as wild birds. Gary Hayward, chairman of Broughshane Environment Wildfowl and Wildlife Trust, described the incident as a nightmare. Hayward described the USPCA and the Northern Ireland Environment Agency as instrumental in treating birds and clearing the spill. Inspectors deployed oil-absorbing barriers and other countermeasures as mitigation, seeking to limit the spill's impact. The agency identified the substance as kerosene, a home heating oil, and traced its source to a nearby tank. Although the waterway has improved, further work will continue for as long as it is deemed necessary. Hayward hopes the incident will act as a deterrent to vandalism. Having suffered extensive contamination, the birds were bathed and treated as quickly as possible. The team administered charcoal to help counter some of the toxins the birds may have ingested. Hopes that the birds were past the worst were tempered by uncertainty over how much they may have ingested. The incident has also placed rescue staff under substantial emotional and mental pressure. Birds can conceal illness effectively, meaning that outward signs may become apparent only when it is already too late. Most rescued birds are non-native species, and their return is contingent on the pond being completely cleaned.
